data.title: Ketotifen
data.summary: Antihistamines · H1 antihistamine with mast cell–stabilising properties (benzocycloheptathiophene)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** H1 antihistamine with mast cell–stabilising properties (benzocycloheptathiophene)

## Mechanism of action
- Stabilises mast cells (inhibits calcium influx and mediator release), blocks H1 receptors, inhibits eosinophil accumulation

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic urticaria (adjunct), cholinergic and cold urticaria, physical urticarias
- Mastocytosis (symptom control), allergic conjunctivitis (eye drops), neurofibromatosis-associated itch (trials)

## Dose & formulations
- 1 mg twice daily (start 1 mg at night); children 0.5 mg twice daily (age >3)

## Adverse effects
- Sedation, weight gain (appetite), dry mouth; full effect takes 6–12 weeks

## Contraindications
- Epilepsy (lowers seizure threshold — caution)

## Drug interactions
- Oral hypoglycaemics (reversible thrombocytopenia reported), CNS depressants

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data — avoid.

## Viva points
- Mast cell stabiliser + antihistamine; slow onset; weight gain

_Sources: Khopkar (Mast cell stabilizers/ketotifen); Wolverton 4e ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
